landing.greeting: Hello, I'm Aneesa, founder of a textured word.
story: I built a brand around something I have always cherished: words. It began when I returned home after teaching abroad for almost a decade, and realised I had spent most of my life either teaching, writing, or performing words for others.
I decided I wanted to design a one-stop shop; where students, creators, and authors alike could find me in my own literary haven.
So, I got to work - and have since curated this space for us; a space where connection is made possible through the taught, written, and spoken word.
landing.audience: Whether you’re an English student finding your way through a text, a creator wanting your best ideas shaped into writing that reaches further, or an author or business looking to give new life and voice to the written word — you’re in the right place.
landing.offer: At a textured word, I work across the English spectrum: teaching, repurposing and performing words in all their textured forms.

name.lede: “Texture” was the word I kept coming back to. We already know how the texture of a fabric or a dish changes the way it makes us feel — yet we rarely talk about words that way, even though the right word, in the right place, lands differently on everyone who hears it.
name.mission: a textured word exists to help people learn, shape and voice language with intention — because words aren't flat, they're textured.

services.oneLiner: I identify the gaps holding a student back and build from there, helping them develop the skills and confidence to show what they know.
services.imageAlt: Aneesa writing thoughtfully in a notebook
problem: In a busy classroom, lessons have to keep moving. When a student misses an important step, later work becomes harder and confidence can begin to fall.

The difficulty is often specific: comprehension, exam technique, working within a time limit or knowing how to begin a piece of writing. One-to-one tuition gives us the time to identify it and work on it directly.

aside.heading: Why individual support can help
aside.body: Online resources and classroom support can be useful, but they cannot always respond to the precise gap in front of a student. Individual tuition makes it possible to slow down, try a different explanation and build from a secure foundation.

services.rangeLine: From blending sounds together through to A-Level and its international equivalent, with individual support shaped around the learner.

problem: A book can take years to write. Its characters, tone and rhythm deserve a narrator who will understand the work before stepping up to the microphone.
The right performance should feel true to the text, consistent from beginning to end and engaging for the listener.

aside.heading: Why preparation matters

background.heading: Training and experience
background.body: Back in 2015, when I set up my first voiceover business, Stylish Voice, I had my professional demos recorded with Gary Terzza; channel 4’s continuity host for over two decades. It was under his tutelage that I made my first foray into the voiceover world and began to understand exactly what goes into bringing the very best of your voice into work that eventually spanned across audiobooks, commercials, explainers, IVRs, and much more.

I have also trained with voice coach Gary Terzza and at Derby Academy. My performance experience also includes spoken word with Beatfreeks and university theatre in England and Canada.

about.heading: Aneesa
about.intro: I am an English teacher, writer, and voice artist with 12 years of classroom experience across four countries. My work is grounded in listening closely, identifying what is needed and responding with care.
paragraphs: Discovering that I had a natural knack with the English language from a young age, I then knew that I wanted to use these same words to help others; whether teaching, writing, or performing them. Words have elevated people by allowing them to understand not only themselves, but the world around them, and have granted them real opportunities in their own lives.

My teenage years and early twenties were spent at various acting schools across the Midlands, culminating in my training at the renowned Television Workshop, where I became familiar with auditioning for both plays and casting directors. This fed into my already existent love for theatre and film. During this time, I also performed as a spoken word poet and volunteered my time reading stories in care homes, where I further indulged in my love for performing words and bringing them to life.

From a young age I also knew I wanted to teach abroad and see the world. So upon graduating with a 1st class in English, I initially taught as an English teaching assistant across primary and secondary schools, before teaching English as a second language with the British Council in Egypt, before then moving to Saudi Arabia. I returned to the UK to gain my PGCE before receiving my QTS in Qatar. It was here that I then taught English Language and Literature to 11-18 year olds for 5 years at a private British international school.
From America to Australia; Canada to Croatia; or Morocco to Malaysia - my extensive travels have only ever deep-rooted love for words, culture, and connection.

After years of travel, a textured word is a place where my love for words, literature, analysis and performance can finally come and take root; where I can encapsulate my years wrapped up in all things - and use these skills to help others achieve their own goals; whether for an exam, content, or an audiobook. It is a place that enables me to work with an array of people, all with different goals in mind, but a shared interest in utilising words to get there.
about.portraitAlt: Aneesa resting her chin on her hands beside an anthology of poetry
about.reflectionBody: Outside my client work, I share reading notes, close analysis and reflections on the books and passages that stay with me.
openTo: Brand partnerships with publishers, stationery brands and education companies

Before teaching, I acted, performed spoken word and read novels aloud in a care home. Each experience taught me something about language, interpretation and connecting with an audience.
retired.empathy: As a child, I found time pressure difficult even when I understood the subject. Years later, I needed a teacher to help me learn Arabic despite having access to countless free resources. Both experiences showed me that the right individual support can make all the difference.
retired.authority: I have spent 12 years teaching English across England, Egypt, Saudi and Qatar, working with learners from age six to adult.
retired.teachingBodies: I've taught with the British Council in Egypt, and with The Oxford Partnership in Saudi Arabia — one of several schools under the Colleges of Excellence programme.
why: Classrooms, production schedules and content platforms are designed to serve many people efficiently. That can leave limited space for the needs of one student, the intention behind one book or the individual voice behind an idea.
Working individually creates that space: time to listen, ask thoughtful questions and shape the work around the person or project in front of me.
